newsitem.title: MEXICO: Fausto batters homes in Mexico, downgraded to storm.
newsitem.headline: Fausto batters homes in Mexico, downgraded to storm.

text.p: Hurricane Fausto damaged 1,700 homes as it swept across the southern tip of Mexico's Baja California before being downgraded on Saturday to a tropical storm, officials said.

An American tourist was killed on Friday when he sought to ride out the storm in a trailer park, but there were no other deaths reported, Guillermo Salgado, interior minister in south Baja California state, told Reuters.

The Communications and Transport Ministry said Fausto was downgraded to a tropical storm as it swept across the Gulf of California and landed in the northwestern state of Sonora. Some residents were evacuated in Sonora, but there was no major damage reported.

"There were some 1,700 houses damaged. Some of these houses are very weak. They just blew away," Salgado said, referring to the damage in Baja California. He said the worst damage on the pensinsula was in the western town of Todos Santos, where Fausto first landed.

He said the only reported death was that of the American, named by state news agency Notimex as Erick Hite, 26, of San Diego. He was electrocuted in the San Jose del Cabo-Cabo San Lucas corridor after a light post fell on his trailer.
Salgado said he was killed during heavy wind and rain six hours before the hurricane officially struck on Friday afternoon.
Trees and posts were blown over around the tourist resort of Cabo San Lucas, but there was no major damage. In the state capital, La Paz, the streets were littered with debris and fallen trees.

After churning northeasterly across the Gulf of California, which separates the peninsula from the rest of Mexico, the storm hit Sonora near the town of Alamos, some 800 miles (1,280 km) northwest of Mexico City.
Notimex said some 560 people were initially evacuated from their homes, but most of them later returned. It said there was little material damage and no casualties.
The nearby port of Topolobambo, in the neighbouring state of Sinaloa near the city of Los Mochis, remained closed to all shipping, the Communications and Transport Ministry said.
